newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNS PRO-EU BUT INDIFFERENT, CRITICAL OF EMU - EVA.
newsitem.headline: FINNS PRO-EU BUT INDIFFERENT, CRITICAL OF EMU - EVA.

text.p: Finns have turned slightly more pro-European Union, but are also critical of EU projects like EMU and indifferent to EU affairs in general, the Centre for Finnish Business and Policy Studies (EVA) said on Monday.

"Finns manage to be of many minds at the same time; solidly pro-EU, strongly EU-critical and openly indifferent to union affairs," EVA director Jyrki Haikonen said in a statement with a new EVA survey of Finnish EU views.
"Membership is approved of, but support systems are unfamiliar, expansion is not attractive, EMU raises doubts," EVA summarised the findings in a headline in the statement.

There was a "frighteningly big gap" between the feelings of ordinary citizens and the EU visions of decision-makers, EVA said, adding most Finns personally think they are not clear on where the EU is heading and what it is actually doing.
Nearly half of the 1,300 people surveyed between August 1 and September 17 said Finland should not join Economic and Monetary Union while 23 percent were in favour, EVA said.
But 43 percent agreed with a statement that it would be "fateful" for Finland to remain outside EMU if many other EU countries joined the single currency block, it said.
One fifth of respondents thought the third phase of EMU would start on schedule at the start of 1999. A majority, 52 percent, were undecided.
One fifth of respondents said Finland should support the implementation of EMU, 45 percent were undecided and one third said Finland should not work towards creating the single currency.
